original_abstract.text: Private, personalised language models must run on local consumer devices, where large, frontier models cannot fit, and retaining long contexts is non-trivial. Sequential memory---the key-value (KV) cache---grows linearly with context length, quickly dwarfing the model itself: for Qwen3-1.7B-Base, 200,000 retained entries require 21 GiB, 6.6 times more than the model weights. Yet the KV-cache compression methods we measured fail beyond moderate compression ratios. We introduce Transformer-FSQ, addressing extreme KV-cache compression by replacing standard key and value projections with a finite scalar quantisation bottleneck. Our cache stores a packed vector of discrete integer codes per token, with no per-token quantisation metadata. Converting a pretrained transformer trains only these projections on 0.25 tokens per original parameter. We evaluate Transformer-FSQ against five baseline families on models from 0.6B to 8B parameters. On long-context retrieval (RULER), from 12$\times$ to 97.5$\times$ Transformer-FSQ is the most accurate method we evaluate, across scales. A fused Triton kernel decodes directly from the integer codes; with baselines given their authors' kernels where available, it decodes at $1.01\times$ (95% interval $0.98$--$1.05$) the throughput of native SDPA attention on the uncompressed Qwen3-8B-Base at $32\times$ and $1.54\times$ at $97.5\times$. Extreme KV-cache compression is therefore a practical way to extend how much context a fixed device can hold.
original_abstract.source_title: Transformer-FSQ: Discrete Latents for Extreme KV-Cache Compression

en.text: Transformer-FSQ replaces standard key and value projections with a finite-scalar-quantization bottleneck. Each cached token is stored as packed integer codes without per-token quantization metadata, and adapting a pretrained model trains only those projections. A fused Triton kernel consumes the compressed codes directly. Experiments across 0.6B–8B language models examine extreme compression and long-context retrieval, with strong accuracy relative to evaluated compression baselines. The contribution is extending retained context under a fixed memory budget, not uniformly accelerating every configuration. Applying the approach to persistent user histories would require projection adaptation and recommendation-specific quality checks.

zh.text: Transformer-FSQ 用有限标量量化瓶颈替换键和值投影，将每个缓存位置保存为打包整数编码，不再存储逐位置量化元数据；转换预训练模型时只训练这些投影，融合 Triton 内核直接读取压缩编码。论文在 0.6B–8B 语言模型上评估极高压缩率和长上下文检索，相对所测压缩基线保持较好精度。其重点是在固定显存下保留更多上下文，并非所有配置都更快。用于长期用户历史仍需投影适配与推荐质量验证。

original_abstract.text: Learned sparse embeddings are a powerful alternative to dense retrieval, yet they have fallen behind single-vector and late interaction models. One reason for their limited adoption is that they are notoriously difficult to train, generally requiring very tight conditions to converge. We present a recipe for training Splade-like encoders on modern backbones and data that achieves a better efficiency-effectiveness trade-off. We discuss the role of logit distribution and its impact on the training stability and the final sparsity of the encoder. We also introduce a new per-position fan-out control - a hard cap on how many vocabulary dimensions each position may emit. We further apply a simple vocabulary merging strategy that removes redundant entries - such as case and word-boundary variants of the same word - which are common in cased BPE-based backbones. We apply our recipe to the LateOn backbone and training data, obtaining SPARSEUP, a sparse encoder that reaches 56.4 average nDCG@10 on BEIR-13, the highest we know of among public vocabulary-based sparse encoders below 150M parameters.
original_abstract.source_title: SPARSEUP: Towards Better Recipes for Training Modern Learned Sparse Retrievers

en.text: SPARSEUP develops a training recipe for vocabulary-based sparse retrievers on modern backbones. It studies how logit distributions affect convergence and sparsity, caps the number of vocabulary dimensions emitted at each position, and merges redundant vocabulary variants. Applied to the LateOn backbone and training data, it reports 56.4 average nDCG@10 on BEIR-13 for an encoder below 150M parameters. For scalable retrieval, the useful connection is between stable training, explicit emission sparsity and index cost; the reported evidence concerns text retrieval rather than recommendation ranking.

zh.text: SPARSEUP 改进现代骨干上的词表稀疏检索训练：分析 logit 分布对收敛和稀疏度的影响，限制每个位置能激活的词表维度数，并合并大小写、词边界等冗余词项。应用于 LateOn 骨干与训练数据后，低于 150M 参数的编码器在 BEIR-13 上达到平均 56.4 nDCG@10。可借鉴点是把训练稳定性、显式稀疏约束与索引成本一起设计；现有证据来自文本检索，尚非推荐排序实验。

original_abstract.text: Attention is a major scalability bottleneck in large language models (LLMs), with its computational cost and key-value (KV) memory traffic becoming increasingly prohibitive as context length grows. Sparse attention addresses this bottleneck by restricting each query to a subset of the context, but its effectiveness hinges on identifying relevant regions both cheaply and reliably. Existing training-free methods primarily rely on runtime relevance estimates, with selection dimensionality and granularity typically governed by fixed heuristics rather than the intrinsic interaction structure of pretrained attention heads. We take a different perspective: the query-key operator of each pretrained head defines a characteristic response structure that determines the resolution needed for sparse selection, both across feature directions and across context tokens. Building on this insight, we propose Head-Adaptive Sparse Attention (HASA), a training-free sparse attention framework that jointly adapts selection resolution along these two dimensions. Along the feature dimension, the singular spectrum of each head's query-key operator determines an effective rank, yielding a compact, head-specific response space. Along the sequence dimension, neighboring regions are progressively merged according to the directional coherence of their token responses in this same space, while heterogeneous regions remain separate. Exact attention is then computed using the original full-dimensional KV states of the selected regions. HASA captures 88.1% of dense-attention mass and, compared with UNIQUE, a strong recent sparse-attention baseline, improves accuracy by up to 3.47 and 2.57 points on RULER and LongBench-Pro, respectively, and accelerates self-attention by up to 1.32x, while achieving up to 14.07x speedup over dense attention.
original_abstract.source_title: Attend at the Right Resolution: Head-Adaptive Sparse Attention via Query-Key Interaction Structure

en.text: HASA makes training-free sparse attention selection depend on each pretrained head’s query-key interaction structure. The operator’s singular spectrum determines a compact response space, while neighboring sequence regions are merged according to response coherence. Attention then uses the original full-dimensional keys and values for selected regions. The paper reports improved long-context benchmark accuracy and attention speed relative to a recent sparse baseline. Its practical contribution is joint control of feature-space selection cost and sequence granularity, rather than a fixed token-selection heuristic. Applying this design to long user histories or ranking models still requires recommendation-specific evaluation.

zh.text: HASA 根据预训练注意力头的查询—键交互结构选择稀疏计算范围：用算子的奇异值谱确定紧凑响应空间，再按响应方向的一致性合并相邻序列区域；最终仍用选中区域的完整键值计算注意力。论文在长上下文基准上报告了相对近期稀疏方法的精度与注意力加速收益。主要价值是同时调整特征选择维度和序列粒度，减少固定选择规则的局限。能否用于长行为序列或排序模型，仍需推荐实验验证。

original_abstract.text: Large-language-model decode attention streams the key-value (KV) cache for every generated token. Packing that cache into 2-bit or 4-bit quantized integers reduces memory traffic but does not automatically translate into latency saving. Existing 2-bit fused kernels reach under 31%/15% of peak HBM throughput on H100/B200. Converting each value and applying its scale and offset before feeding Tensor Cores is a major bottleneck because instruction-issue throughput is scarce on modern GPUs. Instead of applying scale and offset to each KV value, FOSCAR uses affine folding to apply them to the other operand or the output of decode-attention matrix products, depending on the quantization scheme (token-wise or channel-wise). This reduces scale-and-offset operations by up to two orders of magnitude while preserving the dequantized attention output in exact arithmetic. FOSCAR also uses bit manipulation to feed KV operands to Tensor Cores efficiently, requiring only 1 and 0.19 ALU instructions per INT2 element on H100 and B200, respectively. Finally, FOSCAR builds warp-specialized GPU pipelines for Hopper (H100) and Blackwell (B200) using wgmma and tcgen05. On H100, FOSCAR INT2 and INT4 kernels achieve geo-mean speedups of $3.36\times$ and $2.83\times$ over FlashInfer BF16, and $2.03\times$ and $1.71\times$ over TensorRT-LLM FP8. On B200, the corresponding INT2 and INT4 speedups are $2.67\times$ and $2.30\times$ over FlashInfer BF16, $1.48\times$ and $1.28\times$ over TensorRT-LLM FP8, and $1.16\times$ and $1.00\times$ over TensorRT-LLM NVFP4. We integrate FOSCAR into SGLang to benchmark serving efficiency. On long-context serving workloads, FOSCAR increases peak aggregate throughput by up to 170% and 341% over 2-bit and 16-bit baselines, respectively. We open-source FOSCAR as a kernel library at this https URL.
original_abstract.source_title: FOSCAR: Accelerating Decode Attention over 2- and 4-Bit KV Caches through Affine Folding

en.text: FOSCAR accelerates decode attention over two- and four-bit KV caches by moving quantization scales and offsets into the other matrix operand or the output, rather than dequantizing each element separately. This affine folding reduces instruction overhead while preserving the dequantized result in exact arithmetic. Hardware-specific pipelines target Hopper and Blackwell GPUs, and an SGLang integration evaluates long-context serving. The distinction between kernel speed and end-to-end throughput matters when interpreting its gains. The technique is relevant to bandwidth-limited generative recommendation serving, but recommendation-specific quantization quality and serving performance remain untested.

zh.text: FOSCAR 针对二比特、四比特 KV 缓存解码，把量化尺度和偏移折叠到矩阵乘法的另一操作数或输出，减少逐元素反量化的指令开销；在精确算术下保持反量化后的计算结果。实现分别优化 Hopper、Blackwell 流水线，并接入 SGLang 测试长上下文服务。评估时应区分内核加速与端到端吞吐。它对带宽受限的生成式推荐服务有参考价值，但现有实验没有验证推荐负载的速度或低比特质量。

original_abstract.text: Recommendation systems often enter a new serving window before enough outcomes are available to retrain the deployed model. We study this regime with 0.05-1.0% target feedback, a range that spans our stress tests while keeping supervision far below the degrees of freedom of the source recommender. At this scale, existing fine-tuning and meta-learning methods still estimate target-specific updates from extremely sparse feedback, leaving the update direction weakly identified. SAGE-PAIR instead transfers a source-supported residual correction space and only calibrates this space using target outcomes. We introduce SAGE-PAIR, a staged adapter that pretrains a low-dimensional global residual on an adjacent source period and adds a soft router over residual experts conditioned on source user profiles. Target feedback then calibrates this residual state rather than relearning the recommender. On a locked test split of KuaiSAR-v2, SAGE-PAIR (Full) achieves a 1.77% relative improvement in NDCG@10, while a core-protocol comparison shows a further 0.25% gain from routed experts beyond source-pretrained PAIR. Matched source-pretrained LoRA and Adapter-Tuning baselines remain near the source model, supporting the need for a different adaptation space. Thus, SAGE-PAIR improves ranking quality with millisecond-scale adaptation and inference costs. Sparse-feedback adaptation is fundamentally governed by the identifiability of the update space rather than by label count alone. Source pretraining supplies estimable correction directions for scarce labels, while user-conditioned routing contributes a consistent, differentiated cross-user correction on top of the global correction. Our code is available at this https URL.
original_abstract.source_title: SAGE-PAIR: Source-Pretrained Routed Residual Adaptation for Sparse-Feedback Recommendation

en.text: SAGE-PAIR adapts a recommender to a new serving window with only 0.05–1.0% target feedback. It pretrains a low-dimensional residual correction on an adjacent source period and adds user-conditioned routing over residual experts; scarce target outcomes calibrate this existing correction space. On a locked KuaiSAR-v2 test split, the full method reports a 1.77% relative NDCG@10 gain over target-only PAIR. A separate core-protocol comparison isolates a further 0.25% gain from routed experts. It suggests reducing adaptation degrees of freedom before spending scarce labels, with evidence limited to the evaluated protocol.

zh.text: SAGE-PAIR 面向新服务时段只有 0.05%–1.0% 目标反馈的推荐适配。它先在相邻源时段预训练低维残差修正，再按用户特征路由到残差专家；少量目标反馈只校准已有修正空间。在固定的 KuaiSAR-v2 测试集上，完整方法相对仅用目标数据的 PAIR，NDCG@10 提升 1.77%；另一套核心协议对比中，专家路由比源预训练 PAIR 再提升 0.25%。其启发是先限制适配自由度，再使用稀缺反馈，结论限于所测协议。

original_abstract.text: The key-value (KV) cache dominates memory capacity and bandwidth in long-context LLM serving. While 4-bit microscaling formats (NVFP4, MXFP4) shrink the cache and run attention on FP4 Tensor Cores, a fundamental gap remains between algorithmic quantization and system-aware acceleration: existing FP4 KV systems use vanilla quantization that causes severe accuracy drops, whereas accuracy-oriented 4-bit algorithms rely on vector codebooks whose lookup overhead degrades decoding throughput. We present BitDecoding-FP4, an algorithm--system co-design for accurate and efficient native FP4 KV decoding. We mitigate three error sources: Dual-Residual Query Quantization splits queries into two FP4 tensors, cutting query logit error from 60% to 1%; Underflow-Aware Probability Scaling prevents E4M3 scales from rounding long-context probabilities to zero; and Outlier-Aware Key Quantization combines static smoothing, Hadamard rotation, and scale search to suppress key outliers under token-wise scaling. At the system level, we remove the softmax bottleneck via transposed softmax with fused probability quantization and stacked query MMA on paged KV caches. Across dense and MoE models with GQA and MLA, BitDecoding-FP4 stays within 0.5 points of BF16 KV accuracy with NVFP4 (1 point with MXFP4), and tracks BF16 KV in RL training rollouts. In end-to-end serving on NVIDIA B300 with Qwen3-4B and Qwen3-30B-A3B, it delivers 2.4-3.0$\times$ higher peak serving throughput than BF16 KV. The implementation is available at this https URL.
original_abstract.source_title: BitDecoding-FP4: Native FP4 KV Cache Decoding via Algorithm-System Co-Design

en.text: BitDecoding-FP4 co-designs quantization and GPU kernels for native FP4 KV-cache decoding. It separates queries into two FP4 residual components, rescales attention probabilities to avoid underflow, and suppresses key outliers through smoothing, rotation, and scale search. A fused transposed-softmax implementation supports paged caches. The paper evaluates dense and MoE models with GQA and MLA and reports close-to-BF16 quality; B300 serving experiments on two Qwen3 models show higher peak throughput. These hardware- and workload-specific results suggest techniques for low-bit generative recommendation, but do not demonstrate recommendation accuracy or serving gains.

zh.text: BitDecoding-FP4 联合设计量化方法与 GPU 内核：把查询拆成两份 FP4 残差，缩放注意力概率以避免下溢，并结合平滑、旋转和尺度搜索处理键向量离群值；融合的转置 softmax 支持分页缓存。论文覆盖采用 GQA、MLA 的稠密和 MoE 模型，报告接近 BF16 的质量，并在 B300 上用两款 Qwen3 模型验证峰值服务吞吐提升。这些结果受硬件与负载条件约束，生成式推荐的准确率及服务收益尚待验证。

original_abstract.text: Modern Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) inference is constrained by GPU memory. This constraint is mitigated by expert offloading, which stores part of the model's weight in host memory and executes on demand. Though MoE architecture has computation sparsity, more GPUs are needed for serving increasingly larger frontier models. However, existing expert offloading systems overlook this need and fail to scale performance with additional GPUs. We present AdaOffload, a general and efficient multi-GPU hybrid expert execution framework that effectively handles heterogeneous hardware and workloads. We co-design GPU-CPU parallelism and GPU-CPU co-execution for decode and prefill with online workload observation that adapts to different hardware, workload, and batch size heterogeneity. We evaluated AdaOffload on five different platforms with varying GPU capability (L4, Pro6000, B200), number of GPUs, CPU capability, and NUMA topology on three different frontier open-weight models (284B to 753B). AdaOffload achieves $1.9\times$ to $15.5\times$ throughput speedups across different models over state-of-the-art systems.
original_abstract.source_title: Multi-GPU MoE Inference with Adaptive Expert Offloading

en.text: AdaOffload combines GPU-CPU parallelism and co-execution for MoE prefill and decoding, adapting online to hardware, batch sizes and workload differences. Unlike offloading policies tied to one device, it targets scaling across multiple GPUs and heterogeneous NUMA configurations. Evaluations on five platforms and three 284B-753B open-weight models report 1.9-15.5x throughput speedups over the compared systems. Its placement and scheduling ideas are transferable to memory-limited sparse ranking models; these are not CTR measurements.

zh.text: AdaOffload 在 MoE 预填充和解码中结合 GPU-CPU 并行与协同执行，根据在线观测适配硬件、批量和工作负载差异，并考虑多 GPU 与不同 NUMA 拓扑。论文在五个平台、三个 2840 亿至 7530 亿参数开放权重模型上报告了相对所比较系统 1.9–15.5 倍的吞吐加速。其放置与调度思路可供受内存限制的稀疏排序模型参考，这些数值并非 CTR 实验结果。

original_abstract.text: Large recommendation models (LRMs) improve recommendation performance by scaling behavior sequence length, model capacity, and training compute. However, the return on investment (ROI) of continued scaling deteriorates as marginal gains diminish and long-sequence encoding costs rise, especially when this computation is repeatedly executed by distinct models for diverse recommendation stages and business scenarios. To address this issue, we propose SepLRM, a recommendation foundation model (RFM) paradigm that identifies reusable sequence encoding and reorganizes multiple end-to-end (E2E) LRMs into one RFM and multiple independently optimized vertical models (VMs). The RFM adopts an encoder-decoder architecture and exports its final-layer encoder state as the shared key-value (KV) cache that is independent of downstream task-offered candidates. Unlike candidate-specific logits or aggregated user embeddings, the KV cache preserves fine-grained behavioral information. Separation at this native KV interface also allows each VM to construct candidate-conditioned queries while retaining the same query-KV interaction as its E2E counterpart, enabling high-fidelity capability transfer. To ensure both transfer effectiveness and system efficiency, we co-design cache compression, the training and serving workflows, and LG-Store, a distributed storage system for KV caches. Experiments on three large-scale datasets show that SepLRM achieves state-of-the-art offline performance with a transfer rate of approximately 100%. It also demonstrates strong transferability across model iterations, recommendation stages, and business scenarios. Deployment in two large-scale industrial scenarios substantially improves the ROI of sequence scaling and delivers consistent gains in online A/B tests at ByteDance.
original_abstract.source_title: SepLRM: A Foundation Model Paradigm for Recommendation

en.text: SepLRM avoids repeatedly encoding long behavior histories in separate recommendation stages and scenarios. A shared encoder-decoder foundation model exports candidate-independent, fine-grained key-value states; independently optimized vertical models query that cache with candidate-conditioned queries. Cache compression, training/serving workflows and a distributed cache store are co-designed. The authors report approximately 100% capability transfer on three large-scale datasets and online gains in two ByteDance scenarios. The useful scaling idea is to amortize sequence encoding across downstream models while preserving candidate-specific interaction, rather than transfer only an aggregated user embedding.

zh.text: SepLRM 把多个推荐阶段、业务场景反复执行的长历史编码集中到一个基座模型。基座输出与候选无关的细粒度键值缓存，各下游模型再用候选相关的查询读取，并配套设计缓存压缩、训练服务流程和分布式存储。作者在三个大规模数据集上报告约 100% 的能力迁移率，并在字节跳动两个场景中取得线上收益。对扩模的借鉴是：共享昂贵的历史编码，同时保留候选与历史的细粒度交互，而不只传递一个汇总用户向量。

original_abstract.text: A generative recommender names each candidate with a short token sequence, a Semantic ID, and recommends by generating those tokens. Some generative recommenders, including the Uber Eats search engine we are building, write a whole results page, stores with their menu items, in one decoding pass. Every Semantic ID on such a page must name a real store or item that is eligible for the search, such as a store that delivers to the user's location, and that is not already on the page. Each item must also belong to the store above it. A trie over the catalog keeps identifiers real, but eligibility and repetition change with every request and token, and the grammar-constrained decoder we tried could not enforce these changing rules exactly and quickly. We call this constraint LEGIT, for live eligibility gating over identifier tries. Numbering trie leaves depth first turns each rule into a range lookup over one store trie and one item trie, and every generated page passes an independent catalog check. On one NVIDIA B200 GPU with one or two requests per decode step, a direct implementation that walks the trie on the GPU makes each token about 5 times as slow as unconstrained decoding. Across 36 implementations, hardware counters and ablations are consistent with kernel launches and CPU-GPU waits as the source of this slowdown. Our fastest implementation walks the trie on the CPU while the GPU runs the model, needs no custom kernel, and cuts time per output token by 65.9 percent against the direct GPU implementation, to about 1.7 times the unconstrained cost. This implementation is also the fastest on a page layout that puts each item before its store.
original_abstract.source_title: LEGIT: Live Eligibility Gating over Identifier Tries for Constrained Decoding of Heterogeneous Pages

en.text: LEGIT enforces request-dependent eligibility, non-repetition and store-item relationships while a generative recommender produces a heterogeneous results page. Depth-first numbering of identifier-trie leaves turns constraints into range lookups. In tests on one B200 GPU with one or two requests per decoding step, overlapping CPU trie traversal with GPU model execution reduces time per output token by 65.9% relative to direct GPU traversal, to about 1.7× unconstrained decoding cost. It illustrates how host-device scheduling can make exact, changing candidate constraints cheaper; the reported benefit is specific to the tested workload.

zh.text: LEGIT 在生成“店铺＋商品”整页结果时，实时约束候选资格、去重和商品所属店铺。它对标识前缀树的叶子做深度优先编号，把约束转为区间查询。在单张 B200、每个解码步骤一至两个请求的测试中，让 CPU 遍历前缀树并与 GPU 模型计算重叠，较直接在 GPU 上遍历减少 65.9% 的每词元耗时，总成本约为无约束解码的 1.7 倍。它说明精确候选约束的服务成本可通过主机与设备调度降低，收益范围仍限于文中测试负载。

original_abstract.text: High-precision text reranking is a critical component in modern search, recommendation, and agentic retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems. We present Yuanbao-Reranker, a family of general-purpose dense rerankers spanning 0.6B, 4B, and 8B parameter scales built upon the Qwen3 backbone. To construct diverse and reliable ranking supervision at scale, we pair answer-first and query-type-guided document-grounded synthesis with a three-stage curation funnel that verifies positive support, eliminates semantic redundancy, and enforces balanced source-by-length quotas. For each curated pair, we screen real retrieval pools with a teacher score margin to filter out potential false negatives and sample Hard, Medium, and Moderate negative tiers, yielding 2.75M $1{:}3$ ranking groups. We train the models by jointly optimizing pointwise relevance cross-entropy and a bounded minimum-gap hinge objective over both positive--negative and negative--negative pairs. This formulation transfers fine-grained teacher preferences across candidate tiers without over-constraining well-separated predictions, supporting both cross-scale and same-scale distillation followed by layerwise adaptive model merging. Across five comprehensive benchmarks spanning Chinese (CMTEB-R), multilingual (MMTEB-R), English (BEIR), long-document (MLDR), and code (MTEB-Code) retrieval, Yuanbao-Reranker consistently leads every parameter tier: the 0.6B variant reaches 70.96 Avg. to surpass 1B--4B active-parameter baselines, the 4B variant reaches 73.63 Avg. to outperform the 8B teacher (72.68), and the 8B variant achieves a state-of-the-art 74.21 Avg., with substantial gains generalizing across distinct first-stage retrievers.
original_abstract.source_title: Yuanbao-Reranker: Document-Grounded Synthesis and Preference Distillation for Text Reranking

en.text: Yuanbao-Reranker combines document-grounded synthetic supervision, quality filtering and teacher-margin negative selection to train 0.6B, 4B and 8B dense rerankers. A joint pointwise and bounded pairwise loss transfers preferences across candidate tiers, followed by adaptive layer merging. Across five text-retrieval benchmark groups, the authors report strong results at every tested scale, including a 4B model outperforming its 8B teacher on the aggregate score. Its relevance to CTR scaling is a data-curation and distillation recipe for smaller ranking models; the reported evaluations concern text retrieval rather than CTR prediction.

zh.text: Yuanbao-Reranker 结合基于文档生成的监督数据、质量筛选和教师分数差引导的负样本选择，训练 0.6B、4B、8B 三档稠密重排模型。联合点式损失与有界成对损失传递不同候选层级间的偏好，再进行自适应分层模型合并。作者在五组文本检索基准上报告各档模型的较强表现，其中 4B 模型的汇总得分超过 8B 教师。对 CTR 扩模可借鉴数据筛选与小模型蒸馏方法，但这些结果来自文本检索，尚非 CTR 预测验证。

original_abstract.text: Query-Key Normalization (QK-Norm) is widely adopted in modern large language models to control the growth of attention logits and improve training stability. However, query and key norms are not merely sources of instability. The query norm controls the sharpness of the attention distribution, while the key norm determines how strongly a token attracts different queries. These norms therefore carry token-specific information about attention selectivity and token importance. By normalizing both, QK-Norm suppresses this information. This raises a natural question: can we control query-key representations without discarding their sensitivity to magnitude? To address this question, we propose QK-MAP, a Magnitude-Aware Projection for constructing queries and keys. Rather than removing magnitude through normalization, QK-MAP transforms the input representation using multiple learnable frequencies, so that changes in magnitude are encoded as bounded phase patterns. This allows magnitude to be represented through phase and direction rather than vector length alone. Its periodic features have a fixed norm while remaining sensitive to magnitude changes, separating magnitude encoding from norm growth. Multiple frequencies further help distinguish magnitudes and reduce periodic ambiguity. Experiments across model scales from 190M to 7B parameters show that QK-MAP achieves lower training and validation loss than both Standard attention and QK-Norm. Further analyses show that QK-MAP preserves sensitivity to input scale, assigns less attention to the first token, and produces stronger attention contrast for relevant evidence in synthetic long-context tests. These results demonstrate that query-key scale can be effectively controlled without sacrificing token-specific magnitude information.
original_abstract.source_title: Large Language Models without QK-Normalization

en.text: QK-MAP controls query-key scale without discarding token-specific magnitude information. Multiple learnable frequencies encode changes in magnitude as bounded phase patterns, keeping periodic features at fixed norm while preserving scale sensitivity. Models from 190M to 7B parameters achieve lower training and validation loss than standard attention and QK-Norm, with additional synthetic long-context evidence. The design suggests an alternative to normalizing away query/key magnitudes in scalable ranking Transformers; transfer to recommendation remains untested.

zh.text: QK-MAP 用多个可学习频率，把查询与键的幅值变化编码为有界相位模式，使周期特征保持固定范数，同时保留输入尺度信息。论文在 1.9 亿至 70 亿参数模型上得到低于标准注意力和 QK-Norm 的训练、验证损失，并做了合成长上下文测试。它为扩展排序 Transformer 提供了保留查询、键幅值信息的另一种设计，推荐场景仍需验证。

original_abstract.text: Sparse attention accelerates long-context decoding by reading a subset of the KV cache, but existing methods are open-loop: the kernel commits to its selection with no signal indicating whether enough attention mass was preserved and no recovery path when it was not. The needed signal already exists inside the kernel. The fraction of softmax mass on the selected tokens, which we call coverage, satisfies an exact algebraic equality with per-step output error and serves a dual role as the acceptance criterion and the interpolation weight for recovery. Coverage-Verified Sparse Attention (CVSA) turns coverage into a training-free, closed-loop verify-then-correct decode loop that accepts high-coverage drafts and recovers only the heads that fall short, with no sampling, no draft model, and no speculative-decoding infrastructure. Quality varies by only $0.14$ points across the threshold sweep; budget and scheduling ablations characterize the deployed operating point. On LongBench at 7B and 70B, CVSA comes within $1.13$ points of dense attention, statistically matching it at 70B, and it loses $0.8$ points on RULER; measured median decode-step speedup reaches $6.21\times$ at 128K context.
original_abstract.source_title: Coverage-Verified Sparse Attention: Closed-Loop Quality Control for Long-Context LLM Decoding

en.text: Coverage-Verified Sparse Attention adds a verify-and-correct loop to long-context decoding. It uses the softmax mass covered by selected tokens to decide whether to accept sparse attention and how to recover deficient heads. Evaluations at 7B and 70B parameters report near-dense benchmark quality and a maximum measured median decode-step speedup of 6.21x at 128K context. This suggests quality-aware compute allocation for long behavior sequences; the reported results are from language-model decoding rather than recommendation.

zh.text: CVSA 在长上下文解码中加入“核验后修正”：用所选 token 覆盖的 softmax 质量判断是否接受稀疏注意力，并只修复覆盖不足的注意力头。论文在 70 亿和 700 亿参数模型上报告了接近密集注意力的基准质量，128K 上下文下实测中位解码步加速最高为 6.21 倍。其质量感知计算分配可供长行为序列建模参考，但这些收益来自语言模型解码实验。

original_abstract.text: Weight-activation quantization can reduce the memory and compute cost of neural-network inference, but recent methods often require expensive optimization and architecture-specific propagation of basis transforms across layers. We introduce MACaQ, an MXFP4 W4A4 post-training quantization method that treats every linear layer independently. MACaQ applies a per-channel scale and a block-Hadamard transform online to each layer's activations, while absorbing the corresponding inverse transforms into its weights. Retaining these transforms online avoids cross-layer dependencies and enables a simple streaming implementation of the quantization process, in which only one layer must reside in memory at a time. To improve over round-to-nearest quantization, we introduce Flip-Refinement, a Hessian-aware coordinate-descent procedure that greedily moves individual FP4 codes to adjacent representable values. Despite executing the activation transforms at inference time, MACaQ adds only 2.3% end-to-end overhead over pure MXFP4 on Qwen3-32B in vLLM. MACaQ reaches lower perplexity than DuQuant++ and MR-GPTQ, and already matches their best perplexity on Llama-3-8B in 11 times less quantization time. We further apply MACaQ without architecture-specific modifications to an image diffusion model, illustrating the generality of its layer-local design and show quantization of a 122B parameter model in 64 minutes, using only 32.5GB GPU RAM.
original_abstract.source_title: MACaQ: Fast, Model Agnostic Calibrated Quantization for Low-Precision Weights and Activations

en.text: MACaQ performs MXFP4 weight-activation post-training quantization independently for each linear layer, retaining activation transforms at inference while absorbing inverse transforms into weights. A Hessian-aware coordinate-descent step refines FP4 codes, and the layer-local design enables streaming quantization. It matches the compared methods’ best Llama-3-8B perplexity with 11x less quantization time and reports 2.3% transform overhead on Qwen3-32B in vLLM. This offers a practical low-memory conversion path for large ranking models, pending task-specific quality validation.

zh.text: MACaQ 对每个线性层独立做 MXFP4 权重与激活量化：推理时保留激活变换，将对应逆变换吸收到权重中，再用 Hessian 感知坐标下降细化 FP4 编码。逐层处理支持流式量化。论文以约十一分之一的量化时间达到对比方法在 Llama-3-8B 上的最佳困惑度，并在 vLLM 的 Qwen3-32B 上测得 2.3% 的变换开销。这为大型排序模型提供了低内存转换路线，任务质量仍需验证。

original_abstract.text: Click-through rate (CTR) prediction is a core component of recommendation and advertising systems. Large language models (LLMs) offer rich semantic priors that improve prediction quality, particularly in cold-start and long-tail settings. Injecting a full-scale LLM into a CTR pipeline is, however, prohibitively expensive at inference time: existing LLM-enhanced CTR methods avoid this cost by caching LLM outputs offline rather than serving the LLM online. We propose a resource-efficient pipeline, SlimFM, that makes online LLM-based semantic modeling practical: (1) dependency-aware structured pruning compresses LLaMA3-8B by 44% to a 4.5B-parameter backbone; (2) LoRA-based field-aware fine-tuning trains the pruned model to produce discriminative field-level semantic embeddings from lightweight textual prompts; (3) a semantic-guided fusion module injects these embeddings into the feature interactions of a conventional CTR model. Across four datasets and six CTR backbones, SlimFM retains over 99% of uncompressed-model accuracy while reducing inference latency by up to 3.4x relative to existing LLM-enhanced baselines.
original_abstract.source_title: Slim Foundation Models for Latency-Critical Recommendation Serving

en.text: SlimFM makes online LLM-derived semantic features more affordable for CTR prediction. It structurally prunes LLaMA3-8B to 4.5B parameters, uses field-aware LoRA tuning to produce semantic embeddings, and fuses those embeddings into a conventional CTR model’s feature interactions. Across four datasets and six CTR backbones, the authors report retaining over 99% of uncompressed-model accuracy and up to 3.4× faster inference than the compared LLM-enhanced baselines. The compression-and-fusion recipe offers a way to trade semantic-model capacity against online ranking cost.

zh.text: SlimFM 用压缩和特征融合降低 CTR 预测在线调用语言模型的成本：将 LLaMA3-8B 结构化剪枝至 4.5B 参数，用面向字段的 LoRA 微调生成语义向量，再融入常规 CTR 模型的特征交互。作者在四个数据集、六种 CTR 骨干上报告保留未压缩模型超过 99% 的准确性，较所比较的语言模型增强基线实现最高 3.4 倍推理加速。可借鉴的是压缩语义骨干与下游交互模块的联合设计，以权衡语义模型容量与在线排序成本。

original_abstract.text: Advances in large language models and semantic IDs (SIDs) have brought generative retrieval (GR) into industrial applications. These systems must return items that satisfy request metadata constraints as well as relevance requirements. A catalog trie ensures SID validity, but filtering metadata only after generation wastes computation on rejected candidates and may leave too few eligible results. We propose RoutingTrie to incorporate metadata constraints before beam selection. RoutingTrie maintains one shared SID trie and builds a compact index for each metadata field using Dense Bitset or Sparse List. We derive a storage cost formula to guide the choice between these index representations for different field distributions. During decoding, field probes determine whether requested values occur below candidate edges and produce a combined mask that guides beam selection. Experiments on ShopTrie, our configurable synthetic benchmark, demonstrate compact storage and efficient CPU and GPU probing across diverse metadata distributions. In a production replay, RoutingTrie raises Hit@100 from 67.5\% to 96.1\%, a gain of 28.6 percentage points, with only 1.1 ms latency increase. We will release the ShopTrie generator, benchmark scripts, and RoutingTrie CPU and Triton GPU implementations to support reproducibility.
original_abstract.source_title: RoutingTrie: Metadata Routing for Constrained Generative Retrieval

en.text: RoutingTrie applies metadata constraints before generative retrieval selects its beam, avoiding wasted generation and too few valid results from post-filtering. It shares one semantic-ID trie and chooses dense bitsets or sparse lists for per-field indexes using a storage cost model. Probes mask candidate edges during decoding. Experiments cover synthetic metadata distributions and a production replay, where Hit@100 rises from 67.5% to 96.1% with 1.1 ms additional latency. It provides a serving design for scalable constrained retrieval; replay evidence is distinct from an online A/B test.

zh.text: RoutingTrie 在生成式召回选择束搜索候选之前检查元数据约束，减少生成后再过滤带来的浪费和有效候选不足。它共享一棵语义 ID 前缀树，并依据存储成本为各字段选择稠密位图或稀疏列表，在解码时屏蔽不符合条件的分支。除合成数据实验外，生产流量回放中的 Hit@100 从 67.5% 提升到 96.1%，延迟增加 1.1 毫秒。可借鉴的是把约束索引接入生成路径；流量回放结果不能等同于线上 A/B 测试。

original_abstract.text: E-commerce catalogs increasingly live in lakehouse tables: Apache Iceberg metadata over Parquet files in object storage. Product search, however, still runs on copies of that catalog, in a lexical engine and a vector database, each with its own ingestion pipeline, schema, staleness window and bill. We show that search applications can be hosted directly on the data lake, with the lakehouse table as the single system of record. We extend Apache Pinot, a real-time OLAP engine that already serves Iceberg tables in place, with BM25 relevance scoring over its Lucene text index, corpus-wide term statistics so that scores are comparable across files, and reciprocal rank fusion in plain SQL; a real-time table fed by a stream can sit behind the same table, merged by the broker. On the Amazon ESCI benchmark (1.2M US products, 22,458 test queries), hybrid search served from the lake matches exact retrieval (nDCG@10 .361). The lake table is queryable 149 s after its files are registered, and a lake commit is searchable in 3.8 s, close to indexing directly into a search engine. On a brand-sorted lake of 277M products (0.8 TB), one 16-vCPU node answers brand-scoped vector, BM25 and client-fused hybrid searches in 6.5-9 ms (p50), sustains 1,100 vector and 635 BM25 searches per second at under 180 ms p99, and makes a commit searchable in 4.3 s. Search adds only its indexes: no copy of the catalog, no sync pipeline and no second schema, which cuts storage, rebuild time and the operational work of keeping copies consistent.
original_abstract.source_title: Hybrid Product Search Without the Copy: Lexical, Semantic and Filtered Retrieval Served Directly from a Data Lake

en.text: This system serves lexical, vector and filtered product search directly from Iceberg/Parquet lakehouse data through Apache Pinot, adding BM25 statistics and rank fusion without copying the catalog into separate search databases. It matches the reported exact-retrieval quality on Amazon ESCI and evaluates a 277-million-product, brand-sorted lake on one 16-vCPU node. Its scaling value is reduced duplication and synchronization work alongside measured search latency and data freshness. The large-lake latency figures concern brand-scoped queries, not unrestricted search over every product.

zh.text: 这项系统工作通过 Apache Pinot 直接在 Iceberg/Parquet 数据湖上提供词法、向量和带过滤条件的商品搜索，补充 BM25 统计与排序融合，无需把完整目录复制到独立检索数据库。它在 Amazon ESCI 上达到文中精确检索的质量，并用单台 16 核虚拟 CPU 节点评估包含 2.77 亿商品、按品牌排序的数据湖。扩展价值在于减少数据副本与同步工作，同时测量搜索时延和数据新鲜度；大规模实验的低延迟结果针对品牌范围内查询，不代表全目录无约束搜索。

original_abstract.text: Activation sparsity can reduce FFN weight traffic during single-user LLM decoding, but active channels must be identified early enough to avoid fetching unused weights. In pretrained SwiGLU models, training-free routing with the native gate performs substantially worse than routing with the up activation at high sparsity. We show that this ordering reverses after sparsity-aware training. Based on this insight, we introduce SGA-Sparse, which converts pretrained SwiGLU LLMs into fixed-budget activation-sparse models by training the existing gate projection directly as a top-k router. SGA-Sparse updates all model parameters end-to-end while preserving the original SwiGLU activation and introducing no auxiliary router parameters. After approximately 30B training tokens, LLaMA models from 1B to 8B achieve uniform per-token 75-85% FFN channel sparsity while remaining within 0.2-2.7 pp of their original dense checkpoints in average zero-shot accuracy. Because post-training quantization degrades sparsity-trained checkpoints, we further study two complementary quantization-aware training (QAT) recipes: continued-QAT largely recovers performance at 4-bit weight quantization, while joint-QAT performs better for the more aggressive sub-4-bit target. To compare activation sparsity with dense low-bit quantization, we translate the sparsity-induced reduction in weight traffic into an equivalent bit-width. Under this unified weight-traffic metric, our 2.5- and 1.5-bit-equivalent models establish a new accuracy-traffic Pareto frontier: the 2.5-bit-equivalent models match dense 3-bit QAT accuracy, while the 1.5-bit-equivalent models approach dense 2-bit models and outperform dense ternary models by 1.3 pp on average. These results establish native-gate training as a practical approach for combining high FFN sparsity with low-bit weights.
original_abstract.source_title: SGA-Sparse: Training Native SwiGLU Gates for Activation-Sparse and Low-Bit LLMs

en.text: SGA-Sparse trains the existing SwiGLU gate as a fixed-budget top-k router, updating all model parameters without adding a separate router. After about 30B training tokens, 1B-8B LLaMA models retain 75-85% FFN channel sparsity with a 0.2-2.7 percentage-point average zero-shot accuracy gap to their dense checkpoints. Quantization-aware training helps combine sparsity with low-bit weights. The work informs sparse ranking-model FFNs, but its bit-equivalent comparison measures weight traffic, not realized end-to-end latency.

zh.text: SGA-Sparse 直接把已有 SwiGLU 门控训练为固定预算的 top-k 路由器，不增加独立路由参数，并端到端更新模型。约 300 亿训练 token 后，10 亿至 80 亿参数 LLaMA 模型达到 75%–85% 的 FFN 通道稀疏度，平均零样本准确率与原密集模型相差 0.2–2.7 个百分点；量化感知训练进一步帮助结合低比特权重。方法可供稀疏排序模型参考，但文中的等效比特比较衡量权重流量，不等于实测端到端延迟。

original_abstract.text: Long-context applications, long-lived agents, and multi-agent systems require large language models (LLMs) to process and retain extensive information. In these settings, the KV cache can exceed GPU high-bandwidth memory (HBM) capacity, necessitating offloading to host memory, where CPU-to-GPU transfers can dominate inference latency. While KV cache compression can reduce data movement, query-agnostic compression that guarantees accurate attention for arbitrary queries is extremely challenging, if not impossible. We introduce VerKV, a hybrid approach that provides $(\epsilon, \delta)$ guarantees for approximating attention on any given query. VerKV maintains a compact set of query-agnostic pivotal tokens on the GPU, together with a token-level sketch of the full KV cache, while retaining the complete cache in CPU memory. We introduce a novel stochastic sampling procedure, PoissonComp, to select the pivotal tokens. At inference time, our proposed KVFetch algorithm uses the pivotal tokens and the sketch to estimate the relative error of the resulting attention computation. If the estimate satisfies a user-specified $(\epsilon, \delta)$ tolerance, inference proceeds without accessing host memory. Otherwise, VerKV performs query-aware retrieval to fetch additional tokens from the CPU, refining the attention computation to meet the required tolerance. Thus, VerKV enables attention with bounded approximation error while minimizing CPU-to-GPU transfers. We show that PoissonComp outperforms state-of-the-art approaches to KV cache compression. Combined with KVFetch, it achieves near-dense performance (90-100% of dense quality at 32K context length, averaged over RULER and LOFT), using Qwen3-4B, Qwen3.5-9B and Ministral-3-8B, while reducing the GPU memory footprint by 8-32x and keeping CPU-to-GPU memory fetches within 2-23% of the cache per generated token, depending on the model.
original_abstract.source_title: Verify Before You Fetch: Reliable KV Cache Compression for LLM Inference

en.text: VerKV keeps pivotal tokens and a compact sketch on the GPU while retaining the complete KV cache in host memory. It estimates attention error for each query and fetches additional tokens only when the configured error tolerance is not met. On three language models at 32K context, evaluations averaged over RULER and LOFT retain 90-100% of dense quality while reducing GPU cache memory by 8-32x. Query-dependent verification is relevant to long-sequence serving, though the recommendation setting and its transfer costs require separate evaluation.

zh.text: VerKV 在 GPU 上保留关键 token 和紧凑摘要，在主机内存中保留完整 KV 缓存。每次查询先估计注意力误差，只有不满足设定容差时才补取更多 token。在三个语言模型、32K 上下文的 RULER 与 LOFT 平均结果中，它保留了密集模型 90%–100% 的质量，并把 GPU 缓存内存降至原来的 1/8–1/32。按查询核验再取数的方式可用于长序列服务设计，推荐效果和传输成本需另测。

original_abstract.text: Offloading model state to host memory and streaming layer weights let a single multi-GPU node train large mixture-of-experts (MoE) models. GPU memory then becomes a performance budget, shared by resident expert state, retained activations, and execution worksets. The best allocation depends on the expert execution path, batch size, and sequence length. We present OOM (Offload-Optimized MoE), a full-parameter MoE training system that co-designs expert execution and memory allocation. For expert-parallel execution, OOM updates resident experts on their owning GPUs and jointly plans state residency and MoE activation retention according to pipeline dependencies. For local execution, OOM bounds GPU worksets through dependency-aware partitioning; in hybrid models, it also retains attention results on the host to avoid costly recomputation and selectively regenerates layer boundaries through cheaper layers to make room. Calibrated cost models guide joint configuration within GPU and host budgets to minimize step time; OOM selects among the configured paths through short executions. On four H100s, OOM trains with 1M-token contexts, whereas FSDP2, ZeRO-Offload, and MegaTrain exhaust GPU memory at 512K. It also trains a 122B-parameter MoE model, on which all three exhaust host memory. On four 24 GB RTX 4090s, it trains 512K-token contexts and 1,024 1K-token sequences per step without gradient accumulation. Across matched-global-batch comparisons, OOM delivers 1.58x and 4.08x geometric-mean (up to 2.14x and 7.77x) throughput over CPU-offloaded FSDP2 on the two platforms while using the least host memory among the evaluated systems -- as little as 1/3.0 of FSDP2's.
original_abstract.source_title: OOM: Offload-Optimized Full-Parameter MoE Training via Memory-Execution Co-Design

en.text: OOM jointly plans expert execution, resident model state, retained activations and temporary worksets for CPU-offloaded MoE training. Cost models and short trial executions select configurations under GPU and host-memory budgets. On four H100s, it separately demonstrates training with 1M-token contexts and training a 122B-parameter MoE; matched-batch comparisons show geometric-mean throughput gains over CPU-offloaded FSDP2 on H100 and RTX 4090 platforms. The resource-allocation design can inform sparse recommendation training, but the evaluated workloads are language models.

zh.text: OOM 联合规划 CPU 卸载式 MoE 训练中的专家执行、常驻模型状态、保留激活和临时工作区，用成本模型和短试跑选择满足显存、主机内存预算的配置。它在四张 H100 上分别展示了百万 token 上下文训练和 1220 亿参数 MoE 训练，并在 H100、RTX 4090 平台的同批量比较中提高了相对 CPU 卸载 FSDP2 的几何平均吞吐。资源分配思路可供稀疏推荐训练参考，已验证工作负载仍是语言模型。

original_abstract.text: In expert-parallel Mixture-of-Experts serving, a layer finishes only when the most loaded GPU of its group does. Token routing shifts at every decode step and concentrates on a few experts, so most of the group's reserved GPU time waits on stragglers. Recovering that time means re-deciding, at every layer of every decode step, how each replicated expert's tokens divide between its copies. The exact linear-program solvers that make this decision optimally take longer than many of the layers they serve, and their working set outgrows GPU shared memory at deployment scale. We introduce Relief, a bidirectional pairwise relaxation that makes the linear program unnecessary, coming within a fraction of a point of the per-step optimum in a few passes of integer halving over the token counts. We build and measure three deployments, CUDA kernels on the serving GPU, the same verified engine on an FPGA over PCIe, and a fixed-function block beside the accelerator. On decode routing from three open MoE families, Relief holds the balance near the per-step optimum at every group size and layer time measured. Scored as effective utilization relative to that optimum, the kernel alone matches or exceeds every deployable scheme at every group size, from the hundred-microsecond layer on. The on-die engine widens that lead at every point, recovering up to 37.3 percentage points over the deployed static placement, while adding 0.02% of a current accelerator's transistors.
original_abstract.source_title: A Per-Step Load-Balancing Engine for Expert-Parallel MoE Serving

en.text: Relief balances token assignments across replicated experts at every decoding step. A pairwise integer-halving relaxation avoids solving an expensive optimization problem online, and the paper evaluates GPU, FPGA and on-die implementations. Its reported utilization improvements concern expert-parallel execution and should not be equated with end-to-end throughput gains. The method offers a hardware-oriented approach to per-step load balancing that could be tested in sparse recommendation serving.

zh.text: Relief 在每个解码步骤重新平衡复制专家之间的 token 分配，用成对整数减半的松弛方法减少在线求解开销，并评估 GPU、FPGA 和片上实现。论文报告的利用率改善针对专家并行执行，不能直接当作端到端吞吐提升。它为稀疏推荐服务提供了逐步负载均衡的硬件实现思路。

original_abstract.text: Language-model agents increasingly run on workstations with a few consumer GPUs, where large mixture-of-experts (MoE) models keep part of their experts in host memory. With existing CPU-GPU engines, these agents get fast prefill or fast decode, not both: this http URL's expert cache skips forward passes of more than 32 tokens to keep the experts of decode cached, so an agent waits 2.1-2.8 s after each tool output, whereas its default layer placement shortens this wait but is 1.5-1.6$\times$ slower in decode. Our key insight is that a short prefill touches too many distinct experts to upload, yet sends 84% of its expert activations (routes) to a stable set of experts that fits in GPU memory. We present Ostinato, a CPU-GPU MoE inference engine that computes these experts on the GPUs in every forward pass without changing what the model computes. Short prefills split their routes, leaving fewer than one of a token's six routed experts per layer to the CPU; long prefills upload each distinct cold expert once; and each decode step runs as one fixed-shape CUDA graph per GPU. On real coding and customer-service agent sessions with DeepSeek-V4-Flash on four RTX 4090D GPUs, Ostinato is the fastest engine in both phases and finishes every session sooner than all six baselines. Against this http URL and KTransformers, it cuts the median wait after a tool output by 22-55% and finishes sessions 1.4-2.5$\times$ sooner.
original_abstract.source_title: Ostinato: Fast CPU-GPU MoE Inference for Local Agents via Resident Experts in Every Forward Pass

en.text: Ostinato keeps frequently used experts resident on GPUs while offloading other MoE work to CPUs. It adapts execution to short and long prefills and uses fixed CUDA graphs for decoding. DeepSeek-V4-Flash agent-session experiments on four RTX 4090D GPUs report shorter waits after tool outputs and faster session completion than evaluated CPU-GPU baselines, without changing model outputs. The execution design may inform limited-memory sparse recommendation deployments, although recommendation workloads were not studied.

zh.text: Ostinato 让常用专家驻留 GPU，其余 MoE 计算由 CPU 协作承担；它分别处理短、长预填充，并用固定 CUDA 图执行解码。在四张 RTX 4090D 上运行 DeepSeek-V4-Flash 的智能体会话实验中，相比所测 CPU–GPU 基线，工具返回后的等待和会话完成时间缩短，模型输出保持不变。这种执行方式可供显存受限的稀疏推荐部署参考，尚未验证推荐负载。

original_abstract.text: Generative recommendation models represent items as sequences of discrete tokens known as semantic IDs. Existing approaches derive these identifiers using residual or hierarchical vector quantization, assuming that tokens carry independent semantic meaning across quantization levels. Revisiting this assumption, we argue that semantic IDs should behave as hierarchical paths where each token's meaning is conditioned on its prefix. This highlights a mismatch between conventional fixed-codebook quantization and the hierarchical structure implicitly learned by generative recommenders. Motivated by this insight, we propose Adaptive Silhouette Tree (AST), a top-down divisive clustering method that constructs semantic IDs as paths within a tree structure. Unlike prior methods with fixed branching factors, AST dynamically determines the number of branches at each node by maximizing the silhouette coefficient, enabling finer partitions in dense regions and compact groupings in homogeneous ones. We further introduce constrained variants that enforce minimum probability mass during splitting to improve supervision for long-tail items. Extensive experiments on five Amazon Review datasets of varying sizes and domains show that AST significantly outperforms strong baselines. These results demonstrate that aligning semantic ID construction with the inherent hierarchical structure of generative recommenders leads to more effective recommendations.
original_abstract.source_title: Not All Branches Are Equal: Adaptive Semantic ID Construction for Generative Recommendation

en.text: Adaptive Silhouette Tree constructs semantic IDs as hierarchical paths whose tokens depend on their prefixes. Instead of a fixed branching factor, top-down clustering selects each node’s branching count using the silhouette coefficient; constrained variants maintain minimum probability mass to strengthen long-tail supervision. The authors report improvements over strong baselines on five Amazon Review datasets. The transferable design insight is to adapt identifier capacity to local item structure before scaling a generative recommender, rather than assume fixed-codebook quantization matches every region of the catalog.

zh.text: Adaptive Silhouette Tree 将语义 ID 构造成逐层路径，让每个词元的含义依赖此前的前缀。自顶向下聚类依据轮廓系数选择各节点的分支数量，而非固定分叉数；受约束版本还要求分支具有最小概率质量，改善长尾监督。作者在五个 Amazon Review 数据集上报告优于较强基线。对生成式推荐可借鉴的是先让标识容量适应商品空间的局部结构，再扩展模型，而不假设固定码本划分适合所有区域。

original_abstract.text: User sequence modeling is widely used in recommendation and advertising. Search ranking presents an additional challenge: the current query expresses immediate intent, while a candidate product determines which parts of a user's long-term history are relevant. We present a production sequence framework for sponsored-product ranking that augments recent behavior with two retrieval channels over long-term history: candidate-nearest-neighbor retrieval and query-nearest-neighbor retrieval. The selected actions are encoded together with dedicated query and candidate context tokens, while candidate-aware early fusion injects the candidate into every history token. Offline ablations show that dual retrieval improves major ranking metrics relative to the production baseline. In an online A/B test on sponsored-product search traffic, the model increased CTR, attributed conversion rate, and orders per impression.
original_abstract.source_title: Query- and Candidate-Aware Long User Sequence Modeling for Sponsored Product Ranking in Search

en.text: This sponsored-product ranking framework supplements recent actions with long-term history retrieved through two channels: nearest neighbors of the current query and of the candidate product. Dedicated query/candidate tokens and candidate-aware early fusion condition the selected behavior sequence. Offline ablations improve ranking metrics over the production baseline, and an online A/B test increases CTR, attributed conversion rate and orders per impression. It offers a practical way to select relevant portions of long histories before applying a more expressive ranking model.

zh.text: 这项商品广告排序方法用两条检索通道补充近期行为：分别寻找与当前查询、候选商品相近的长期历史。选出的行为与专用查询、候选词元一起编码，并在早期融合阶段把候选信息注入每个历史词元。离线消融优于生产基线，线上 A/B 测试提升 CTR、归因转化率和每次曝光订单数。它为长历史提供了实用的相关片段选择方法，再由表达能力更强的排序模型处理这些片段。

original_abstract.text:
Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) inference with expert parallelism (EP) relies on All-to-All communication, making computation-communication overlap strategies critical for achieving high performance. However, no strategy is universally optimal. Across 103 production configurations, varying input lengths, and four hardware platforms, we observe that the fastest strategy shifts based on model shape, EP degree, input length, and hardware. Since no strategy dominates more than 80.6% of configurations, configuration-aware selection is necessary.
In this work, we propose OverlapAdvisor, which models overlap stages using two granularities to capture computation-communication dependencies. OverlapAdvisor builds a unified performance model, accounting for deviations from peak compute, memory, and communication performance across workloads and hardware. This model enables launch-time, configuration-aware strategy selection within two serving engines. We conduct experiments on four MoE models (30B-235B) against three baselines, utilizing SGLang and vLLM. At the kernel level, OverlapAdvisor achieves 1.16x average and 1.59x maximum speedups, with a prediction MAPE of 3.3%-15.9%. In SGLang and vLLM, it improves end-to-end throughput up to 31.7%. Its granularity-guided optimizations further achieve median speedups of 1.10x for DeepEP-v1 and 1.22x for FlashMoE.
original_abstract.source_title: OverlapAdvisor: Modeling and Adapting Computation-Communication Overlap for Distributed MoE Serving

en.text: OverlapAdvisor models compute-communication dependencies at two granularities to select an overlap strategy for expert-parallel MoE serving. The preferred strategy changes with model shape, expert-parallel degree, input length and hardware, so selection happens at engine launch rather than relying on one fixed strategy. Tests of four 30B-235B models on four platforms report up to 31.7% end-to-end throughput improvement in SGLang and vLLM. This is a useful systems design for distributed sparse recommendation, with transfer gains still unmeasured.

zh.text: OverlapAdvisor 用两种粒度建模计算与通信依赖，在引擎启动时为专家并行 MoE 选择重叠策略。最佳策略会随模型形状、专家并行度、输入长度和硬件改变，不能固定使用同一方案。论文在四个平台、四个 300 亿至 2350 亿参数模型上测试，SGLang 和 vLLM 的端到端吞吐提升最高为 31.7%。这种按配置选择策略的设计可供分布式稀疏推荐参考，迁移收益尚未测量。
